# System Design Simulator

Two linked MIT-licensed workbenches for learning system design:

- Simulator: individual-request discrete-event simulation with finite slots,
  queues, retries, measured latency percentiles and failure injection.
- System Design Lab: deterministic approximate traffic-day simulation,
  82 practice problems, 41 lessons, 99 building blocks, cost/reliability/
  latency/data-safety scoring and candidate-led timed interviews.

The simulator retains 33 component types, 24 worked examples, 18 challenges,
6 educational incident stories, a 48-step learning path, 119 glossary entries,
diagram editing, saved designs, file/image exports and presentation mode.

The learning workbench retains the complete practice and lesson catalogs,
clarification/estimation/drawing workflow, daily challenges, sandbox, replay,
reference designs, interview defenses and local progress.

## Limits and privacy

The engines use different formats and models; their latency/cost definitions
cannot be equated. Neither is a production benchmark or cloud bill guarantee.

Default deployment is static and account-free. Optional account sync, public
leaderboards and encrypted short-link backends are implemented but not
configured in the default build. GitHub Pages cannot host those APIs.
Local progress, fragment links and file exports remain usable.

Default simulator fragments are encoded, not encrypted. Anyone with the
complete link can read them. Configured encrypted short links instead store
ciphertext and carry a browser-only key in the fragment. Never put secrets in
diagrams or share URLs.
